note: Editorial decisions about existing graph connections. These are pedagogical judgments against the stated curriculum scopes, not Ministry-mandated prerequisite chains or teacher-moderated reviews. Original source archives remain unchanged.

reviews.reason: Recognising observable physical and chemical changes in Year 6 does not require the later Year 10 account of atoms and compounds.
reviews.replacementReason: Observing whether a change makes a new substance can provide an example to explain later using atoms and compounds.
reviews.locator: Science PDF p. 14, Year 6 Physical Science; p. 24, Year 10 Physical Science

reviews.reason: Year 9 work on the periodic table does not require the full Year 10 compounds topic. Atomic number already has its own earlier association.
reviews.replacementReason: Recognising elements and their symbols in the periodic table can help when studying compounds made from different elements.
reviews.locator: Science PDF p. 24, Years 9–10 Physical Science

reviews.reason: The original variation topic includes broader genetics and statistical distinctions. Year 8 natural selection can begin with heritable differences without requiring that full topic.
reviews.locator: Science PDF p. 21, Year 8 Biological Science; p. 29, Year 10 Biological Science

reviews.reason: The Year 8 introduction to natural selection does not require a prior molecular account of genetic mutation.
reviews.replacementReason: Understanding selection among inherited differences can help connect later discussion of genetic mutations to how traits become more or less common.
reviews.locator: Science PDF p. 21, Year 8 Biological Science; p. 29, Year 10 Biological Science

reviews.reason: Year 7 division of a whole number by a unit fraction can be reasoned about by counting equal units; multiplication of two fractions is a broader Year 8 skill.
reviews.locator: Mathematics and Statistics Phase 3 > Number > Number structures and operations, Year 7 and Year 8 practices

reviews.reason: Year 7 division of a unit fraction by a whole number can be modelled by equal sharing without first mastering the broader Year 8 multiplication of fractions.
reviews.replacementReason: Sharing a unit fraction into equal parts can be revisited as taking a fraction of a fraction when learning multiplication.
reviews.locator: Mathematics and Statistics Phase 3 > Number > Number structures and operations, Year 7 and Year 8 practices

reviews.reason: A learner can add and subtract within 20 using objects and pictures before memorising all number facts within 20.
reviews.replacementReason: Using objects or pictures to build addition and subtraction facts can support later fluent recall of those facts.
reviews.locator: Mathematics and Statistics Phase 1 > Number > Operations, first and second years at school
